match.reason: The closest bank point is written for Year 12 Physics and covers red shift and the CMB as evidence, but it does not give the 13.8 billion year age or the sequence of atoms, stars and galaxies forming, so adapting it would need new content and a change of depth.

draft.title: The big bang theory
card: The big bang theory says the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago. It started from an extremely hot, dense state.
The big bang was not an explosion in a place that already existed. Space itself has been expanding since then.
As the universe expanded, it cooled. Once it was cool enough, atoms could form.
Over a very long time, gravity pulled gas together into stars and galaxies.
draft.remember: The universe began hot and dense, then expanded and cooled, which let atoms, stars and galaxies form.

a.q: Which statement best describes the universe soon after the big bang?
opts: It was extremely hot and dense
It was cold and filled with stars
It was cool and made of galaxies
It was empty space with no heat
a.why: The theory says the universe began in an extremely hot, dense state. Stars and galaxies came much later, after the universe had expanded and cooled.
a.clue: Think about the state the universe started in.

b.q: Dev says atoms formed in the universe before it had cooled at all. Using the big bang theory, what is wrong with his idea?
opts: Atoms could only form once the universe had cooled enough
Atoms formed only after the first galaxies had formed
Atoms formed because the universe stopped expanding
Atoms were already there before the big bang began
b.why: The theory says the universe cooled as it expanded, and atoms formed once it was cool enough. Galaxies formed later still, so atoms did not need galaxies first.
b.clue: Which came first, cooling or atoms?

a.best: It was extremely hot and dense

b.best: Atoms could only form once the universe had cooled enough

problems.detail: The right option says atoms 'could only form' once cool enough, but the card says 'Once it was cool enough, atoms could form'. 'Only' is stronger than the card's wording. Better: 'Atoms could not form until the universe had cooled enough'.

check.summary: The facts are accurate and both questions have one clear answer. The only issue is that question b's right option adds 'only', which is stronger than the card's 'could'.
